newsitem.title: INDIA: India tribal guerrillas execute six Hindus.
newsitem.headline: India tribal guerrillas execute six Hindus.

text.p: Tribal guerrillas executed six Hindus after tying them to a tree in northeastern India in the latest attack in their separatist campaign, police said on Tuesday.

Members of the militant National Democratic Front of Bodoland (NDFB) kidnapped seven Bengali-speaking Hindus in Assam state late on Monday and took them to a forest in Tuslibari, about 40 km (25 miles) west of Guwahati city near the Bhutanese border.
They tied the hostages to a tree and fired at them, police in Guwahati said. Six were killed and the seventh was seriously wounded and was now in hospital, police said.
The NDFB, formed in 1985, wants an independent homeland for 600,000 Bodos carved out of the oil- and tea-rich state.
The guerrillas have their camps in the foothills of southern Bhutan and accuse Bengali-speaking Hindu immigrants of encroaching on their homeland in Assam.
The NDFB and other guerrilla groups have recently stepped up their separatist campaigns.
On Monday, more than 400 passengers escaped unhurt when suspected guerrillas of the Bodoland Liberation Tigers Force set off a bomb by remote control on a rail track in Assam.
Six coaches were derailed in the blast, which police said occurred several minutes before the Delhi-bound Rajdhani Express reached the spot.
Bodo guerrillas have killed 11 people in the past two weeks in Assam with remote-control bombs. At least 33 people died last December when Bodo extremists bombed a train.
Monday's attack comes ahead of a planned 36-hour general strike from Wednesday in support of a call by Bodo student groups campaigning for a separate Bodoland.
